bullets.title: 10yr yield at 5.33%, S&P/Nasdaq at ATHs but breadth weak; Russell 2000 in -7.8% drawdown
bullets.body: The 10-year UST yield rose ~5-6bps to 5.33-5.34%, highest since 2002, while S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit new all-time highs. Despite record index levels, Russell 2000 ended lower and weak breadth persists — small-caps in a -7.8% drawdown since Quad2 started. S&P futures were mixed pre-market (+0.38% per one source, -0.19% per another), reflecting cross-currents from higher oil and rates.

bullets.title: Q3 earnings setup bullish: 29.5% EPS growth expected, all 11 S&P sectors positive
bullets.body: JPM models 26Q3 earnings at 29.5% growth and 12.3% revenue growth with record positive pre-announcement rate; all 11 S&P 500 sectors expected to show positive revenue and EPS growth. Median S&P500 earnings grew +15% YoY with highest NTM estimate revisions since COVID. Broadening beyond Mag7/AI theme anticipated, with non-AI plays gaining traction.

bullets.title: Fed repriced higher: 71% Dec hike odds, modal path 4.50-4.75% by mid-2027; rate stabilization key for long-duration
bullets.body: Fed path was repriced sharply — 71% odds of a December hike, modal path implying three additional hikes to 4.50-4.75% by mid-2027. The 2-year Treasury rose ~50bps to 4.84% over the past month; 10-year crossed 5.30%. However, October hike odds fell from 64% to 22% intraday, and bond yield stabilization is viewed as more supportive for long-duration growth equities.

bullets.title: SpaceX raising $40B (Apollo-led) to buy NVIDIA Rubin chips — largest single AI infrastructure financing yet
bullets.body: SpaceX is pursuing ~$40B in financing ($10B bank loans + $30B investment-grade debt, led by Apollo) exclusively to purchase Nvidia Rubin chips for AI infrastructure; deal expected to close in 2027. The transaction reinforces the AI compute demand narrative but raises circularity concerns given Nvidia's $500B funding platform involvement with Apollo, BlackRock, and KKR. SpaceX 2056 bonds trading at ~$0.85, flagging underlying financial stress.

bullets.title: AI capex sustainability requires $400-600B ARR by end-2027; hyperscaler bond issuance now 14% of net Treasury supply
bullets.body: Investor consensus holds that $400-600B in AI frontier-lab ARR by end-2027 is needed to justify capex through 2028-2029, with a path to ~$1T annual AI revenue by 2028-29 required for 15%+ ROIC. Hyperscalers' bond issuance now represents 14% of net new Treasury borrowing, competing directly with government debt for capital. S&P 500 consensus sees 10yr yields at 5.1% by year-end and S&P 500 above 8000.

bullets.title: BofA flags growing tech bubble risk; Ray Dalio calls AI a 'classic bubble nearing bursting'; advise call spreads
bullets.body: BofA flagged growing tech bubble risk but advised clients to stay invested via call spreads. Ray Dalio separately characterized AI as a 'classic bubble' nearing a bursting point, citing rising rates and heavy AI infrastructure debt load. IGV returned only +2.6% YTD vs S&P 500's +13.7%, with SaaS multiples at 5.9x FY+2 EV/Sales and security at 9.4x.

bullets.title: Oil near $90-$100 on Iran/Houthi escalation and tropical storm threat; API shows crude draw
bullets.body: WTI crude was around $89.85-$90.15 (Nov) and Brent near $101.80 (Dec), supported by Iran escalating Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks (9 in October alone), Houthi tensions, and tropical storm Isaias expected to strengthen to Cat 2 approaching offshore production Saturday. API data showed a 2.09M crude draw vs. consensus expecting a +1.7M build. Higher crude is weighing on equity futures overnight.

bullets.title: Banks hit hard: XLF -6.6% in Sept, major banks -12-14%; flat yield curve, AI deposit disintermediation weigh
bullets.body: XLF fell -6.6% in September vs S&P 500 -0.5%, a -610bps spread, despite Quad 2 historically favorable for financials (78% positive frequency). The flat 2s10s spread (~40bps) compresses net interest margins; JPMorgan non-interest-bearing deposits fell from 30.0% in 2Q22 to 24.6% in 2Q26. Meta's AI agent Muse is flagged as a new threat to deposit stickiness by automating yield-chasing behavior.

bullets.title: Musk clarifies Terafab: Tesla/SpaceX build and operate; TSMC may only sublease; Intel stays as process partner
bullets.body: Elon Musk confirmed his companies (Tesla/SpaceX) will build and operate Terafab, with TSMC limited to potentially subleasing a portion — not an operational role. TSMC fell ~4% in pre-market on the clarification. Intel CEO confirmed Intel remains an active manufacturing partner for Terafab via the 14A process, with $16.8B initial investment and up to $119B total.

bullets.title: MSFT raises Azure prices 17-25% globally starting Feb 1; AWS and neoclouds also hiking
bullets.body: Microsoft is raising Azure VM/Storage prices 17% in Europe and 25% worldwide for legacy v1/v2 services starting February 1. AWS and neoclouds (NBIS, CRWV) have also recently raised prices. The pricing cycle across hyperscalers reinforces AI monetization thesis and supports near-term revenue visibility.

bullets.title: GOOGL power-constrained on AI infra; nuclear deal with CEG adds 890MW new + 2,700MW existing at ~$80/MWh
bullets.body: Google's AI infrastructure lead times are gated by power availability, with the company targeting a 6-month token-serving capacity doubling. Google and Constellation Energy announced an 890MW new nuclear + 2,700MW existing capacity deal in PJM on a 20-year contract with first uprates in 2028; MS estimates ~$2.50/share EPS upside and ~$800M FCF for CEG assuming $80/MWh pricing.

bullets.title: Midterm election outlook: Wolfe takes 'under' on 65% Democratic Senate odds; base case 50-50 or narrow GOP edge
bullets.body: Wolfe Research is skeptical of betting market pricing for Democrats at ~65% favorites to take the 2026 Senate, flagging that Dems would need to flip states Trump won by 11+ points — historically very difficult. Base case is 50D-50R or 51D-49R. Notably, the policy difference between a 'blue House' and 'blue sweep' is described as virtually nonexistent, limiting market catalyst potential.

bullets.title: Macro: ISM Services fell to 54.5 from 55.6 peak but elevated; labor market stable with ~51K monthly NFP
bullets.body: ISM Services eased to 54.5 in September from 55.6 peak but remains well in expansion territory. Labor market is stable with a 3-month average NFP of ~51K and no consumer distress signals. Consumer spending above 2% driven partly by AI's impact on asset prices, according to sell-side consensus.

bullets.title: Semiconductor sector rotation: custom silicon (MRVL, AVGO) gaining vs. memory and semicap equipment
bullets.body: Multiple sources flagged a rotation from memory stocks into custom silicon plays, with DRAM spot prices largely sideways and NAND flash 512Gb TLC down 2.9% WoW. Memory stocks reportedly topped in late June 2026. Semicap complex is leading broader weakness with SOXX ~10% below ATHs, while optical/networking names (CIEN +13.8%, ALAB +7.58%, MTSI +6.81%) rallied on MRVL interconnect commentary.

bullets.title: Micron Taiwan union votes to authorize strike Oct 19 over bonus dispute; 15K employees at risk
bullets.body: Micron's union at its Taoyuan, Taiwan facility voted to authorize a strike (99% member vote among 1,994 members) over a bonus scheme dispute. The union is encouraging members to walk out October 19 if no profit-sharing proposal emerges. Micron employs ~15K in Taiwan across Taoyuan and Taichung operations; company ended negotiations with Taoyuan union in September.

bullets.title: Housing affordability at 40-year lows; mortgage rates above 7%, turnover near multi-decade lows
bullets.body: Mortgage rates above 7% and housing turnover near 40-year lows are creating acute affordability stress across US housing. Morgan Stanley initiated homebuilder coverage with a split view: Toll Brothers Overweight, PulteGroup/D.R. Horton Equal-Weight, NVR/Lennar/KB Home Underweight. Key debate is whether the market is approaching a floor and what catalysts could unlock it.

bullets.title: Meta Personal Agent Protocol (PAP) launch positions agentic commerce as next structural fintech theme
bullets.body: Meta and Sierra are developing the Personal Agent Protocol (PAP), an open standard for AI agent interactions with businesses, with v0.1 launching late October. Meta is testing checkout within Meta AI with Adyen, PayPal, Shopify, and Stripe. Visa and Mastercard are viewed as well-positioned given existing trust infrastructure; Adyen particularly favored via its Orb acquisition and agentic product development.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI spending concerns have abated; Citi rates AMZN/GOOGL/META/MSFT/ORCL Buy with avg 43% upside
bullets.body: Citi views AI spending concerns as resolved, with hyperscalers demonstrating robust cash flow and AI monetization. All five — AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT, ORCL — are rated Buy with an average 43% upside to price targets. Investors need confidence in a path to ~$1T annual AI revenue in 2028-29 to sustain capex cycles through 2030.

bullets.title: TSM expected to beat Q3; Citi raises PT to NT$4,000 on 46% YoY revenue growth and $81-90B capex next two years
bullets.body: TSMC is expected to beat Q3 guidance; Citi raises FY27/28E net earnings 4-5% and target price to NT$4,000 (25x 2027 EPS). Full-year revenue forecast is +46% YoY, with 4Q revenue expected +15% QoQ. TSM capex is projected at US$81B/US$90B over the next two years on strong advanced node demand.

bullets.title: UBS equity strategy: pair high-growth/high-CFROI stocks at 30% P/E discount vs expensive-fundamentals basket
bullets.body: UBS flags a wide valuation dispersion: a higher-growth, high-CFROI basket trades at ~30% P/E discount vs an Expensive Fundamentals basket despite 10pp higher forward sales CAGR and 28pp higher CFROI. The high-growth basket trades at 1.1x PEG on sales CAGR vs 4.6x for expensive-fundamentals. Piper technicals similarly flag pivoting macro strategy toward quality factors: high FCF yield, profitability, strong balance sheets.
